story_type: helicopter rescue school in heavy surf and cliffs
hook: That wall of white water is the classroom.
narration: That wall of white water is the classroom.
Coast Guard pilots, aircrews and rescue swimmers train here, at the mouth of the Columbia River.
A rescue watercraft charges through the break below.
The hoist brings the swimmer back, so the helicopter never touches the water.
Then they move to the rugged cliffs of the Pacific Northwest.
outcome: The students left the school trained for surf and cliff rescues.

location_card.place: Columbia River mouth, near Astoria, Oregon

title: Coast Guard trains in monster surf
description:
In November 2021, Coast Guard pilots, aircrews and rescue swimmers trained at the Advanced Helicopter Rescue School near Astoria and the mouth of the Columbia River, practicing search and rescue in heavy surf and on rugged cliffs.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video by Petty Officer 3rd Class Michael Clark, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/832144/advanced-helicopter-rescue-school-ahrs-fall-2021

facts.source_quote: Coast Guard pilots, air crews, and rescue swimmers from around the Nation attend the Advanced Helicopter Rescue School in November of 2021, in the vicinity of Astoria and the Columbia River mouth.

facts.claim: Training for heavy surf and rugged cliffs
facts.source_quote: Students of the school, designed and held by staff from the Aviation Training Center in Mobile, Alabama, learned skills needed to conduct search and rescue operations in heavy surf and rugged cliffs common of the Pacific Northwest.
